column6: Both paragraphs convey the same theological concept of God's goodness as a motivating force for repentance, emphasizing His willingness to redeem despite sin. The phrasing is different, but the core message remains unchanged.
column7: God's unrelenting goodness, to be willing to redeem us and restore us if we come to Him is a positive agent in our path of repentance. His goodness isn’t that we continue in sin, but that despite our sin He makes a way for us to be redeemed and experience His salvation.
column8: God’s unalloyed goodness—that if we come to Him He is ready to deliver and restore us—is a positive motivator on the path of our repentance.
